title: The Ford Model T debuts, 1908 — from 12½ hours to 93 minutes
sources: Wikipedia: Ford Model T — produced from October 1, 1908; 'I will build a motor car for the great multitude'; at first assembled by hand, only 11 cars built at the Piquette Avenue Plant in the first full month of production; moving assembly line: cars came off the line at three-minute intervals, production time cut from 12½ hours to 93 minutes by 1914; Runabout $825 in 1909, lowered to $260 by 1925; by 1918 half of all cars in the US were Model Ts; Ford: 'Any customer can have a car painted any color that he wants so long as it is black'; from 1908 to 1913 the Model T was not available in black, only gray, green, blue and red

Wikipedia: Henry Ford — Model T debuted on October 1, 1908; $5 daily wage (5 January 1914) more than doubled the rate of most of his workers; paying employees more enabled them to afford the cars they were producing
Wikipedia: Assembly line / Highland Park Ford Plant — moving assembly line began on October 7, 1913, at Highland Park

post.facebook:
On this day in 1908, the Ford Model T made its debut.

Henry Ford had promised "a motor car for the great multitude". But at first, each Model T was assembled by hand — in the first full month of production, his Piquette Avenue plant built just eleven.

In 1913, Ford put the cars on a moving assembly line at Highland Park. A car came off the line every three minutes, and the time to build one fell from 12½ hours to 93 minutes. The price of a Model T Runabout fell from $825 in 1909 to $260 by 1925.

In 1914 Ford more than doubled the pay of most of his workers, to $5 a day — and the men who built the cars could afford to buy them. By 1918, half of all the cars in America were Model Ts.

Ford famously wrote that a customer could have any color he wanted, "so long as it is black". Yet from 1908 to 1913, the Model T wasn't sold in black at all — only gray, green, blue and red.
